title: Machine-learned immune-cell quantification stratifies lung-cancer prognosis
summary: HALO random-forest image analysis quantified immune-cell densities and PD-L1 staining in resected non-small-cell lung cancers from 165 patients. Combined epithelial/stromal CD8-positive lymphocyte density and epithelial PD-L1 proportion were independently associated with disease-free survival. This single-centre retrospective study used manual tissue annotations and did not establish benefit from selecting postoperative treatment by these measurements.
organization: Shizuoka Cancer Center; Shinshu University School of Medicine

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective 165-patient immune-marker measurements and adjusted survival association.
evidence.unknown: Single-centre selection, annotation bias and clinical decision benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: HALO ensembles random forests to distinguish tissue compartments and quantify CD8/Foxp3/PD-L1 signals for prognostic association.
